components.name: Flat Top Navigation
components.description: Three centered 68×48 point buttons sit in a flat full-width strip beneath the native titlebar. Each places a 21pt SF Symbol above a caption label. Only the selected item uses accent-colored content on a native quaternary rounded surface; the group has no enclosing capsule.
components.nativeView: Content HStack of plain Buttons above a Divider

components.name: Selectable Skill Row
components.description: A native selectable inset List row keeps skill name and source to one truncated line, then reserves trailing width for count metadata. Virtualization prevents off-screen directory pages from loading eagerly.
components.nativeView: Tagged row in selectable inset List

components.name: Persistent Skill Detail
components.description: The right HSplitView pane updates in place and scrolls as one page. Metadata uses 6pt row spacing; major sections use 16pt; the pane keeps 24pt horizontal and bottom padding with no top inset.
components.nativeView: HSplitView detail pane with compact edge-aligned vertical ScrollView

components.name: GitHub Repository Installer
components.description: A Browse list control opens a compact native sheet with an owner/repository or github.com URL field, inline validation, shared agent and installation-method controls, and a standard Cancel / Install All Skills footer. Submission transitions directly to mutation progress.
components.nativeView: List control Button and sheet with TextField, agent picker, segmented Picker, and footer actions

components.name: Installed Skill Linker
components.description: A compact native sheet supports both single-skill and batch linking. Single mode summarizes current links; batch mode adds a searchable two-column installed-skill selector filtering by name or recorded repository, with Select Visible scoped to the filtered results. Both use the shared searchable two-column agent picker with empty local selections, preserve existing agents, group execution by recorded source, and transition directly to mutation progress.
components.nativeView: Management-row or detail Button and sheet with skill grid, agent picker, and footer actions

components.name: Agent Target Picker
components.description: Inline filter and adaptive grid of checkbox toggles; the persistent Browse detail gives it a bounded 300pt scrolling region while fixed-width sheets use their available height. A 24pt checkbox is vertically centered beside the two-line agent name and secondary caption-sized global skill directory, with Select Visible and Clear actions.
components.nativeView: TextField and vertically flexible LazyVGrid of full-row Toggle controls using AgentCheckboxToggleStyle

components.name: Installation Method Picker
components.description: Native segmented control for Symlink and Copy with contextual caption help.

components.name: Prominent Mutation Action
components.description: Native bordered-prominent Install or Update action; Install fills the persistent detail width at large control size.

components.name: Confirmation and Summary Feedback
components.description: Native confirmation dialogs protect Install, Update All, and Remove; concise localized alerts summarize search and list failures.

components.name: Skill Mutation Progress Sheet
components.description: Non-dismissible modal progress for installation, linking, update, and removal while the CLI runs, with the exact copyable shell command in a horizontally scrolling monospaced line, followed by action-specific completion status and expanded selectable plain-text CLI output with ANSI terminal formatting removed.
components.nativeView: sheet with ProgressView, horizontal ScrollView, and DisclosureGroup

components.name: Runtime Repair State
components.description: Application-root checking and missing-runtime states that replace the manager until bunx or npx is usable.

narrative.overview:
Skills follows the focused structure of a polished macOS preferences window: the native titlebar stays visually quiet, a flat icon navigation strip sits directly beneath it, and the selected destination appears below. Browse and Installed pair a virtualized skill list with persistent detail while Settings retains a centered grouped form.

The interface defers visual styling to SwiftUI and AppKit conventions so it remains familiar across appearance, accent, accessibility, and language settings.
keyCharacteristics: Flat icon navigation below the native window titlebar
Lazy skill lists beside persistent detail panels
System typography, materials, controls, and SF Symbols
Complete English and Simplified Chinese presentation

rules.name: The Semantic State Rule
rules.body: Green means completed, orange means needs attention, and the destructive role is reserved for removal; never use these roles as decoration.

rules.name: The Dynamic Palette Rule
rules.body: Do not replace system roles with fixed light-mode or dark-mode color values.

rules.name: The Named Style Rule
rules.body: Use SwiftUI text styles instead of hard-coded point sizes so hierarchy follows macOS accessibility settings.

rules.name: The Persistent Detail Rule
rules.body: Browse and Installed keep the selected skill and its controls visible side by side; selecting another row updates the right column in place.

rules.name: The Native Layering Rule
rules.body: Use the platform's container hierarchy before adding a custom background, border, blur, or shadow.

dos: Do use native SwiftUI controls, text styles, focus, keyboard behavior, VoiceOver semantics, and Reduce Motion behavior as the baseline.
Do keep skill selection and its controls visible together in the list and detail columns.
Do pair every semantic state color with an SF Symbol and localized text.
Do preserve technical identifiers, source URLs, paths, and raw output as selectable text where implemented.
Do keep diagnostics available but collapsed until requested.
donts: Don't add custom cards, decorative glass, gradients, fixed palette values, or ornamental shadows.
Don't turn the interface into a terminal transcript or lead with stdout and stderr.
Don't use success, attention, or destructive colors without their native icon, label, or control role.
Don't add custom animation timing where native selection, progress, disclosure, dialog, and content behavior already responds to accessibility settings.
Don't translate native controls into cross-platform approximations or fixed visual recipes.
